findings.finding: NBS household-appliance retail sales improved from deep declines in Q2 to roughly flat in Q3 2026 (July -1.9%, August +2.3%, September +1.9% y/y against June -8.7% and H1 -7.4%), against JD's Q2 electronics & home appliances revenue of -11.8% y/y; consensus (Guosen) already expects JD's electronics decline to narrow only to 'single digits'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Electronics was the line behind the Q2 revenue decline and the -7.3% reaction on 2026-08-13 (Caixin: 'subsidy pullback hits electronics sales', https://www.caixinglobal.com/2026-08-14/jdcom-posts-first-quarterly-revenue-decline-as-subsidy-pullback-hits-electronics-sales-102473925.html).
findings.why_not_priced: Public macro series, so mostly priced; previews (Guosen 'single-digit decline') do not quantify how far the NBS appliance line recovered between Q2 and Q3. If the market had read it as a full recovery, the revenue consensus would sit above management's 'retail back to slight growth' frame and the skew would not lean to puts.
findings.independence: Proxy, macro-to-company. CONTRADICTED IN SIZE by the broader appliance-retail series AVC (all channels, cited by Haier as -10% in Q3 vs -12.4% in Q2), filed as the next finding; the two series disagree on how much appliances recovered, which is why this is sized small.

findings.finding: JD's two largest white-goods suppliers printed weak Q3 2026: Midea revenue -4.12% y/y and Haier -10.1% y/y, and Haier's own release says China's appliance industry fell 10% in Q3 (AVC: Q3 appliance retail RMB 179.1bn, -10% y/y) after the national subsidies ended, against AVC's Q2 decline of 12.4% - i.e. appliances only modestly less bad than the quarter that produced JD's -11.8% electronics line.
findings.link: Midea and Haier are major brands sold through JD's first-party appliance business, which sits inside JD's electronics & home appliances line (RMB 157.9bn in Q2 2026, about 46% of group revenue); AVC is the channel-wide appliance retail series both suppliers cite.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Same electronics line that drove the -7.3% on 2026-08-13.
findings.why_not_priced: Supplier prints from 2026-10-29 in A-share filings that US ADR previews do not cite; previews frame Q3 as the quarter the subsidy base 'gets absorbed'. If priced, the USD revenue consensus would not imply ~+5% group growth above the Guosen +3%.
findings.independence: Haier release https://www.haier.com/about_haier/xinwen/20261029_296008.shtml (2026-10-29) states 'industry Q3 down 10%'; AVC H1 -9.9% with Q2 -12.4% via https://m.gelonghui.com/p/6523174. Shares the appliance question with finding 1 (opposite direction); the two are kept apart because they are different series and net to about -0.2.

findings.finding: Phones were strong in China in Q3 2026: Apple's Greater China revenue for the quarter ended 2026-09-26 rose 21% y/y to $17.54bn and NBS telecommunication-equipment retail sales rose 20.4% / 27.3% / 31.1% y/y in July/August/September, which offsets part of the appliance weakness in JD's electronics line.
findings.link: Apple is a supplier to JD, which is one of Apple's largest authorised online retail channels in China (no revenue-share figure sourced); phones/computers/digital is the other half of JD's electronics & home appliances line alongside appliances.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No line-specific JD reaction found; electronics overall drove the -7.3% on 2026-08-13.
findings.why_not_priced: A supplier print dated 2026-11-02, after JD last spoke (08-13) and after the Goldman note (09-14) in which management said Apple's new products would ship about a month later than last year, making the September base harder - so the management-anchored previews assume a phone drag that Apple's own China number and the NBS September telecom line (+31.1%) do not show. If priced, previews would be pencilling electronics close to flat rather than a single-digit decline.
findings.independence: NBS telecom equipment, independent series: https://www.stats.gov.cn/english/PressRelease/202610/t20261020_1965662.html (Sep +31.1%); Guosen preview also expects phones back to positive growth (https://m.gelonghui.com/news/5326436). Caveat: one summary says Apple's Greater China number missed forecasts (https://digg.com/world-business/iyfp5u0e), and an Apple China beat need not mean JD share gains.

findings.finding: Management restated the Q3 bar inside the quarter: Goldman (2026-09-14, after meeting management, Buy, HK$169) relays that JD Retail revenue growth turns positive in Q3 as the trade-in base fades, general merchandise improves from Q2's 5.6%, food-delivery orders grow sequentially while per-order subsidies fall; this repeats the 2026-08-13 call guidance that JD Retail returns to positive revenue growth in Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On 2026-08-13 the company met/beat profit but missed on the growth narrative and fell 7.3%; no instance found of JD missing an explicit qualitative quarterly guide.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: it is the bar itself. It is filed because a mid-quarter reaffirmation two months after the guide lowers the probability that retail revenue stays negative; if the market doubted it, the skew would be more negative than +3.46.
findings.independence: Original guide on the Q2 call: https://wallstreetcn.com/articles/3779392 (2026-08-13), same management, so the two count once.

findings.finding: The forward commentary carries a sourced Q4 caution: in the same 2026-09-14 Goldman note management said Q4's comparison base eases but electronics ASP inflation (tight supply of high-end phone and PC chips pushing prices up) could hurt demand, and the 2026-08-19 36Kr call summary records component-driven price rises damping upgrade demand in Q2; JD gives no numeric guide, so the next-quarter read comes from this tone.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: JD has no numeric guide; the 2026-08-13 reaction (-7.3%) followed a quarter whose profit beat came with weak growth commentary.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced (target cuts since mid-October). If fully priced, revisions would have moved FY2026 revenue growth below the +2.9% average still shown on 2026-11-09, and Morgan Stanley's Sell would not be the only one cutting into the print.
findings.independence: https://eu.36kr.com/zh/p/3946200786671238 (2026-08-19) on component-driven price increases; shares management as the original speaker with finding 4, but a different claim (Q4 demand rather than Q3 growth).

findings.finding: This ADS sold a clean profit beat on falling revenue last print: Q2 2026 non-GAAP EPS RMB 6.29 vs RMB 5.63 consensus (+12%) with revenue -2.9% y/y, and the ADS fell about 7% on the day (baseline -7.31%); a Q3 that again beats on profit (food-delivery loss narrowing against Q3 2025's RMB 15.7bn peak loss) without a convincing revenue turn is likely to be sold again.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-08-13: EPS beat, revenue decline, -7.3% (US), HK line -10% next session; 2026-05-12 (Q1): +3.14%.
findings.why_not_priced: Reaction function, not a fact the market lacks; filed because the consensus EPS ($0.88) and the whisper ($0.95) frame the print as an EPS event while the last print showed EPS does not carry this name. If the market were positioned for an EPS-driven pop, call skew would be bid; it is the puts that are bid.
findings.independence: Caixin on the same print (https://www.caixinglobal.com/2026-08-14/jdcom-posts-first-quarterly-revenue-decline-as-subsidy-pullback-hits-electronics-sales-102473925.html); baseline history row 2026-08-13 -7.31%.

findings.finding: The sell-side bar was cut into the print: Morgan Stanley Sell $25->$23 (2026-11-09), Mizuho $39->$37 (2026-11-03), Barclays $41->$38 and CMBI $48->$47 (2026-10-14), and Guosen trimmed its forecasts 'slightly on consumer pressure' (2026-10-16); spot $27.59 sits 29% below the $38.84 mean target and the ADS is -2.66% over 5 days.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No source on JD's reaction after pre-print cut cycles specifically.
findings.why_not_priced: Target cuts are public, so the lowered bar is priced in the level; it is filed because a lowered bar slightly raises the chance a merely in-line growth print clears it. If the cuts had not reached consensus, the USD revenue estimate would sit higher than Guosen's by more than it does.

findings.finding: JD closed the Ceconomy (MediaMarkt/Saturn) takeover on 2026-11-12, owning 59.8% (EUR 1,335m consideration) and consolidating Ceconomy's results from that date, so Q4 2026 reported revenue will include about seven weeks of Europe's largest electronics retailer in its peak season; the call is the first chance for management to frame the Q4 top-line with it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior JD reaction to an acquisition consolidation found.
findings.why_not_priced: Five days old and inorganic; street Q4 models may not carry it and any Q4 'growth' commentary will be flattered by it. Most investors will strip it out, so it is small; if it were fully modelled, Q4 consensus revenue would already show a step-up (not found either way). Low-margin retail, so neutral to slightly dilutive on margin.
findings.independence: Gurufocus preview notes consolidation 'starting this quarter' (https://www.gurufocus.com/news/9202309/jdcom-jd-to-report-q3-2026-earnings-amid-retail-recovery-and-acquisition-integration).

findings.finding: Only about $1.0bn remained on JD's $5.0bn buyback (adopted Aug 2024, runs to Aug 2027) at 2026-06-30 after $1.0bn was used in H1 2026 and $3.0bn in 2025, so a top-up or new programme is a plausible announcement with results; JD launched the $5bn programme alongside a results release in August 2024.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No sourced reaction to a JD buyback announcement on a print day.
findings.why_not_priced: An inference, not an announcement; with the stock 29% under its mean target and RMB 235bn of cash and short-term investments, a new authorisation would not be in the price. If the market expected it, a 'buyback' line would appear in previews; none mention it.

findings.finding: Food-delivery competitor Meituan guided that Q3 2026 food-delivery unit economics improve y/y but that 'seasonality and higher subsidies will impact sequential results', which cuts against the preview assumption (Guosen) that JD's new-business loss narrows quarter on quarter from Q2's RMB 9.85bn; the y/y narrowing against Q3 2025's RMB 15.7bn loss is not in doubt.
findings.link: Direct competitor in the same product (on-demand food delivery), three-player market; JD's food delivery sits in its New Businesses segment, which lost RMB 9.85bn in Q2 2026.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: New-business losses: Q2 2026 narrowed y/y (9.85bn vs 14.8bn) and the stock still fell 7.3%, so this line has not paid on the upside.
findings.source_date: 2026-08-28 (Meituan Q2 2026 results; Quartr page shows a conflicting 28 Sep date)
findings.why_not_priced: Previews quote the y/y narrowing (>50%) that management promised; the sequential question is not addressed. If priced, previews would show Q3 new-business losses flat or up QoQ rather than narrowing.
findings.independence: Meituan returned to core profit as competition eased: https://www.morningstar.com/news/dow-jones/202608283006/meituan-returns-to-profit-as-food-delivery-competition-eases-update (2026-08-28) - points the other way (easing competition), which is why this is sized small.

findings.finding: Vipshop guided Q3 2026 net revenue to RMB 20.3-21.4bn, -5% to 0% y/y (below the street), after a -4.3% Q2, signalling soft discretionary online spending in the same quarter.
findings.link: Same channel (China B2C online retail) and overlapping categories (apparel, beauty, home inside JD's general merchandise, RMB 109.2bn in Q2); no shared-customer figure.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: General merchandise slowed to +5.6% in Q2 2026 (from double digits) in the print that fell 7.3%.
findings.why_not_priced: A guide from August, so mostly priced; JD's general merchandise mix is skewed to groceries and supermarket rather than apparel, so the transmission is weak.
findings.independence: NBS daily necessities in Q3 below H1 (finding 13).

findings.finding: NBS staples did not accelerate in Q3 2026: daily necessities +1.8% / +1.8% / +4.1% y/y in July/August/September against +4.4% for H1, grain-oil-food +5.3% / +4.0% / +6.7% against a Jan-Sep +6.8%, while Guosen expects JD's general merchandise to accelerate to high single digits (supermarket near double digits) from Q2's +5.6%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: General merchandise decelerated to +5.6% in Q2 2026; the print fell 7.3%.
findings.why_not_priced: Public macro, but the preview's general-merchandise acceleration is built on JD's share gains rather than the category; if the market doubted it, previews would carry GM at ~5%. Proxy only: JD can gain share in a flat category.
findings.independence: Vipshop's soft Q3 guide (finding 12) - different category mix.

baseline_tension: The evidence nets to a small negative that agrees with the mild put skew (+3.46) and the slightly negative 5-day path, but it is close to balanced (phones up, appliances down, bar lowered by target cuts), so it neither confirms nor fights the option market strongly.
lessons_applied: Rule 5 (narrow proxy vs broad series): the NBS appliance recovery is contradicted in size by AVC's all-channel -10% that the suppliers cite, so finding 1 went from +0.4 to +0.2.
Rule 6 (inside what the company guided): the mid-quarter restatement of 'JD Retail back to positive growth' is the guided bar itself, so finding 4 went from +0.2 to +0.1.
Rules 1 and 7 left standing: the beat-sold reaction (-0.5) and the skew/short-interest check were already in the draft; short interest is low (2.7 days), so no negative was shrunk for squeeze risk.

Rule on FPI reaction history: the baseline's 6-K-matched history is flagged untrustworthy; abs_move was set from the option-implied 5.77% and the two confirmed prints (-7.3%, +3.1%), not from the baseline median, and left at 6.0; p_up left at 47.
